outcome: Help retailers and brands plan, deliver and measure consented retail-media campaigns with transparent inventory, attribution, and brand controls.
overview: Retail media networks in the Gulf are growing faster than the measurement behind them, and advertisers increasingly refuse last-touch numbers they cannot audit. This solution plans and delivers consented on-site and in-store campaigns against transparent inventory forecasts, then measures them with holdout-based incrementality rather than attribution assertion. Audiences are built only from consented data, aggregated to a minimum cohort size, and brand-safety rules block unsafe adjacencies before a placement serves. Exposure, orders and billing reconcile to the same ledger the advertiser sees. A 6–10 week campaign pilot measures delivery completeness, reporting turnaround and incremental sales with stated confidence intervals.

benefits.text: Improve campaign delivery and measurement completeness against forecast inventory
benefits.source: Redington Retail catalogue; consistent with published retail-media measurement guidance
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Effect size to validate on the customer’s own inventory and campaign mix during the pilot — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Reduce post-campaign reporting turnaround and the disputes that follow late or unreconciled numbers
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on ad-server, order and billing data arriving on a reliable schedule and reconciling to one ledger

benefits.text: Quantify incremental sales with an approved holdout design and stated confidence, not last-touch attribution
benefits.source: Reference design — holdout-based incrementality with a documented methodology
benefits.limits: Confidence intervals depend on campaign scale; small campaigns may not reach a readable effect at all

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); consented audience, order and campaign data remain in the customer tenancy in the reference designs

notFor.situation: No consent management or reliable consent records for advertising use
notFor.why: Audiences are built only from consented data; without trustworthy records nothing can lawfully be targeted or measured

notFor.situation: No ability to hold a genuine advertiser or audience holdout
notFor.why: Incrementality is the whole promise; without a holdout the platform can only restate exposure, not prove effect

notFor.situation: No agreed methodology or governance for attribution and reporting standards
notFor.why: Advertisers dispute numbers whose method is not written down; the platform will not publish figures it cannot document

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns consent records, brand-safety policy, advertiser agreements and published measurement standards · Duration: 6–10 weeks pilot; further 14–26 weeks to platform scale
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, measurement lead, data engineer, integration engineer; customer retail-media commercial owner, campaign operations lead, privacy officer, finance and billing owner · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Discovery, consent review and media-revenue baseline
2) Audience, inventory and ad-serving integration
3) Brand-safety rules and measurement methodology configuration
4) Holdout design, power analysis and reconciliation testing
5) Campaign pilot with per-campaign readouts
6) Benefit review, billing audit and handover

Brand-safety filters demonstrated to block prohibited adjacencies before serve
Privacy and security reviews complete and advertiser UAT passed
